crates_created.name: oya-foundry-oauth-subscription-kernel
crates_created.bnf_justification: oya-<microservice:foundry>-<bc:oauth-subscription>-<layer:kernel>; v4.1 conformant; oauth-subscription is a discrete bounded context (PKCE + flow state) separable from oya-foundry-account-runtime; layer=kernel — pure value types + deterministic PKCE handshake + SHA-256, NO I/O (loopback server lives in adapter layer). Departs from the IP-001 plan (`oya-foundry-agent-runtime::foundry::auth.rs`) per ICM scaffold-lock 01KRMC1RRT3KKBPFWST64Q33TZ since no `oya-foundry-agent-runtime` crate exists today; new kernel is a final-shape replacement and avoids a placeholder agent-runtime crate.
crates_created.purpose: PKCE-pinned OAuth subscription-token capture flow. Pure-Rust SHA-256 + base64url-no-pad for kernel layer (avoids dep on sha2/0.10 in kernel — adapter layer can substitute). Tokens never enter the kernel — `record_capture` accepts only a pre-minted `SecretReference` from the secrets-store adapter.
crates_created.linus_good_taste: Eliminated parallel `import_api_key` helper by collapsing API-key import into a `FlowKind::ApiKeyImport` variant of the same entry point; one surface, one decision tree.

symbols_shipped: OAuthError::{InvalidVerifierLength, InvalidVerifierCharset, EmptyAuthorizationEndpoint, EmptyTokenEndpoint, EmptyScopes, EmptyStateNonce, ProviderRejected, LoopbackPortReserved}
open_items: Loopback HTTP server (the listener that receives the OAuth `code`) lives in adapter layer — not in this kernel. The kernel exposes the descriptor; the adapter binds the port.
Browser-open hand-off (operator-console UX) lives in app layer.
